description: Bell-buoy robot referee with a striped whistle arm.

api.auth: Bearer token read from the TRIPO_API_KEY environment variable only; never hard-coded or logged.

prompt: a bell-buoy shaped robot referee mascot character, conical red-and-white striped buoy body and head, standing upright on two short stubby robot legs, one arm ending in an integrated striped whistle nozzle held forward, other arm straight out to the side in a T-pose, full-body T-pose, legs apart and clearly visible, front facing, symmetric, clean metallic robot topology, game-ready mascot character
rig_notes: rig-check flagged riggable=false (rig_type still reported as biped) -- likely a conservative call on the buoy's cone/whistle silhouette rather than a genuine skeleton failure. Proceeded with the requested biped rig anyway (as permitted per Tripo docs, a false riggable result is not always final) and it produced a fully valid, symmetric 41-joint anatomical skeleton -- downstream structural validation (paired left/right limb bones, matching chain depths) found no problems, and the retargeted idle clip is a clean loop. Treat this asset as verified-good despite the prerigcheck warning; a future regeneration could try a clearer T-pose render if a stricter rig is ever wanted.

animation.loop_verification: Computed world-space joint positions via forward kinematics at t=0 and t=duration from the sampled TRS tracks; max bone-position delta between the first and last frame across all named bones was 0.001052 model units (<0.002), i.e. the pose at the end of the clip is effectively identical to the start, so it loops without a visible pop.

mesh.triangle_rule: Sum over every mesh-referencing node's primitives: TRIANGLES=indices/3, STRIP/FAN=indices-2, using indices count when indexed else POSITION count; a mesh with no referencing node counts once.
mesh.pbr: pbrMetallicRoughness with baseColorTexture, metallicRoughnessTexture, and normalTexture all present
mesh.texture_resolution: 2048x2048 (normal map is PNG; baseColor and metallicRoughness maps are JPEG)
mesh.skin: 1 skin, 41 joints, mesh bound via JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 with the node's skin index set
